events.text:
🔥 Pakistan steps up aerial attacks on Afghanistan as new border war risks emerging
📌 [Pakistani air strikes on Afghanistan's Kandahar](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/75055), Paktia and Khost provinces have claimed the lives of at least four people, the Taliban government stated on September 24, vowing retaliation.
🌏 Earlier in the day, Pakistan announced it had struck 10 locations in Afghanistan believed to store and launch drones allegedly used in cross-border attacks.
🌏 OSINT sources on X claim Pakistan may have struck the former CIA Gecko Camp in Kandahar, which was built inside the former compound of Taliban founder Mullah Omar and seized by the Afghan Taliban during the 2021 takeover.
🌏 Pakistani authorities accuse Afghanistan of allowing extremist fighters of the Pakistan Taliban (TTP) and other groups to operate from Afghan territory, conduct cross-border drone strikes and terror attacks. Kabul vehemently denies the accusations.
🌏 On September 21, the Pakistan Air Force raided northeastern Afghanistan, killing three civilians in the Nurgal district of Kunar province, according to Afghan officials. Islamabad says 28 terrorists were eliminated.
🌏 Previously, on September 18, a faction of the TTP claimed responsibility for a terror attack in Kohat, a city in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. The attack killed at least 31 people, according to Al Jazeera.
🌏 Tensions between Pakistan and Afghanistan are rising, threatening a repetition of the February all-out border warfare, which was triggered by Pakistani air strikes against what it called camps belonging to the TTP and the Islamic State-Khorasan Province (ISIS-K). The strikes followed a February 6 suicide bombing in Islamabad.
